notes.title: Get Ready for the BIG 0.8 Update!
notes.notes:
[h3]Greetings Adventurer![/h3]
[hr]Get Ready![/hr]
[h1]⭐ Update 0.8 is JUST around the corner![/h1]

Update 0.8 is currently in the [b]final internal testing phase[/b], and the release is scheduled for THIS month!

Here’s what’s waiting for you in the 0.8 update:

[h2]📝 The New Character Sheets![/h2]

The character and monster sheets have received [b]major upgrades[/b] in version 0.8!
Now, you can roll your attacks, actions, and spells with just one click—including monster actions!

Here’s how it works:

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/7e0f2c4814d67d19eaa86e3aa08270655ab6f0c2.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Select your action and press "Use." The roll-to-hit is automatically calculated for you.
[*] After the to-hit roll, the result window lets you roll damage directly. And yes, critical hits are automatically doubled & the results are posted in the chat for your party members!
[/list]

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/cc037e65291db2604ee409e6a54107d8df4f3a73.jpg[/img]

We've also improved ALL 5e monster sheets that are included in DFD to work with the new improved system! At the same time, we’re continuing to enhance DFD’s automation features, and we plan to add more functionality to the character and monster sheets (e.g., automatic saving throw calculations and damage application). These features are not part of the 0.8 update yet, but we’d love to hear your feedback!

[h2]🧝 The New Beginner’s Story![/h2]

We’re thrilled to announce that the DFD onboarding experience will be [b]fully voice-acted[/b]!
This unique onboarding process introduces new players to the game and helps them learn the ropes.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/5cc78f4ecc31f0435ebe40ee08033e4e5b788236.jpg[/img]
[i]We’ve also hidden some easter eggs in the onboarding experience. Can you find them all?[/i]

We’re excited to hear your thoughts as we plan to add more in-depth tutorials for veteran players and game masters in the future!

[h2]Features, Improvements, Bug Fixes, and More![/h2]

But that’s not all!
We’ve packed a ton of improvements and fixes into 0.8. The full patch notes will be available on release day, but here’s a sneak peek:

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/68c75189da3c62bca509939cefbb4d882cd60e7a.jpg[/img]
[i]More hairstyles? The barber has been busy for the 0.8 update![/i]

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/5d7878750f7b6e0c95bd2f4b2f65711da68d34aa.jpg[/img]
[i]A free saving throw! Based on your feedback on Discord, we’ve added a failsafe for unsaved map changes. Thanks, GM![/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h1]🔔 When Exactly Will Update 0.8 Be Released?[/h1]

Update 0.8 is in its final testing phase and will be released [b]this month[/b]—specifically, within the next two weeks.

Stay tuned as we share more details in the coming days!

As always:
[b]Thank you for your support, and see you inside DFD![/b]

[h3]Discuss this Update on Discord[/h3]

[url=https://discord.gg/e8FznWcyxk][img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/d776b95ce3951c6b6035941e94c532768f156bd1.gif[/img][/url]

notes.title: Sneak Preview: The upcoming Update 0.8!
notes.notes:
[h2][b]Greetings, Adventurer![/b][/h2]

Over the past weeks and months, we've been hard at work on [b]major new features[/b] and various improvements based on your feedback (yes, we're looking at you, Discord community!). Today, we're thrilled to [b]officially announce Update 0.8[/b]!

[hr][/hr]

[h1]🆕 What to Expect in Update 0.8[/h1]

[h2]📝 Rollable, Automated Attacks and Spells[/h2]

One of the most exciting additions in Update 0.8 is the introduction of [b]rollable Attacks and Spells[/b].


[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/08b936d8c840a8a33e0cfb341802dc0f6a20f5ac.jpg[/img][i]Barbarians, rejoice! Even less math needed to play DFD![/i]
[list] 
[*]Want to roll an attack? Just press "Attack," and your proficiency is automatically calculated. 
[*]Need to roll damage? It’s just one click away! 
[*]Casting a spell? The damage roll is automatically determined based on the spell level! 
[/list]We are continuously working on the automation side of things for DFD and we are looking forward to hearing your feedback on these upcoming first steps towards this direction.

[h2]🧝A Singleplayer Mission for Beginners?![/h2]

Wait, what? Singleplayer? Can I now play DFD without a GM? Well... yes and no.

Based on the feedback from our recent Player Survey, [b]many of you have been asking[/b]  for a tutorial. So, in Update 0.8, we've prepared something special just for you:

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/8bc4bc9039af933128b1bfed4756c9c7272f2ec9.jpg[/img]
We've added a [b]brand-new Singleplayer Beginner's Mission[/b] designed to provide new players with an excellent introduction to DFD and its tools!

For our seasoned players, we're also working on adding additional tooltips and information that can be accessed during gameplay.

[hr][/hr]
[h1]🔔When Will Update 0.8 Be Released?[/h1]

Update 0.8 is currently in full-force development, and we're aiming for a release in [b]Q4 this year[/b]—specifically, this November.

Stay tuned as we share more details as we get closer to the release date!

[hr][/hr]
[h1]What Else Can You Expect from Update 0.8?[/h1]

But wait… there's more! You can also look forward to:

[h3]🐺 New Miniatures[/h3]
[h3]🐺 New Character Assets[/h3]
[h3]...and yes, even more features waiting to be unveiled![/h3]

So, keep your eyes peeled on our social media and Discord for sneak peeks of what's to come in Update 0.8.

See you inside DFD!

[h3]Discuss this update on Discord[/h3]

[url=https://discord.gg/e8FznWcyxk][img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/d776b95ce3951c6b6035941e94c532768f156bd1.gif[/img][/url]

notes.title: OUT NOW Q3 Update 0.7.2!
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings Adventurer! [/h1]

Kicking off Q3 with a bang, we are incredibly excited to release the [b]new  0.7.2 Version[/b] for Dungeon Full Dive!

Without further ado let's get into this update's content:

[h1] 🆕New Features[/h1]
[list]
[*][h2]🌐Visual Grid Tool[/h2] 
The new visual grid tool makes combat even easier by allowing you to display a [b]5-foot grid[/b] on [b]any map.[/b]
[*][h3] Toggleable visual grid [/h3]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/16ec8aef3d1942c9900133851397297f3203bc52.gif[/img]
[*][h3] Automatically Measure Distances when moving your miniature [/h3]
Additionally, you can also enable the new "Auto Meassure" feature, to start measuring distances for any objects that you pick up. Neat!
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/35eabe156fcb2eac6b1a2116070e12886e5b8ec9.gif[/img]
[/list]
[h1] 🆙 Feature Improvement[/h1]
[list]
[*] [h3]📏Improved Readability for the Ruler [/h3]
The ruler has been improved for better readability. The distance text now scales depending on the distance to the player to be larger when farther away. Additionally, a new outline font is used for better readability
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/043ff343465c69de264f769f4c4ad4f1438c4a12.gif[/img]
[*][h3]🅰️Improved Readability for Context Menu & Dice Results:[/h3]
The texts used in both areas now also use the new outline font for better readability.
[/list]
[h1] 🧝New Character Assets[/h1]
With the new [b]0.7.2 Update[/b], we have added even more versatility to the character editor! 
[list]
[*][h3] New Beard [/h3]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/110240485c0f6b819acdf051e90d7031f7ec2ca7.png[/img]
The new beard allows for some [i]elegant [/i] variety.
[*][h3] New Eyebrows [/h3]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/9bdf299f36cf88715baad7004417be7089a16b03.png[/img]
[/list]
[h1] 🔧 Fixed Issues [/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug, where some network matches were terminated after a short time period due to server issues.
[*] Fixed a bug, where miniatures made with the character editor could fall through floor when picked up during mapbuilding.
[*] Displaying the game on the second screen will no longer stop when closing the sidebar, while inside "Streaming Mode" on Desktop PC. Previously closing the sidebar (or fulldiving into a miniature) would stop the "Streaming Mode" which was not intended.
[/list]

[h1]🫵Your Review matters![/h1]
And as always: Thank you so much for your support and playing DFD!
If you want to support the game, please leave a review on our Steam Page. It helps us and the game immensely!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2839600/Dungeon_Full_Dive_Player_Edition/

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1710740/Dungeon_Full_Dive_Game_Master_Edition/

notes.title: May Update #3 Version 0.7.1-586
notes.notes:
[h2]Greetings Adventurer![/h2]
 
yes, yet another update is being released this week! ✨
 
With 4 new assets for the character editor as well as a variety of bug fixes & improvements, your next sessions this weekend are about to get even more versatile!

Here is what's in this week's update:

[h2]🎨 New Character Editor Assets[/h2]

[h3]2 new Hairstyles[/h3] 
A new hairstyle that will make your character become the main protagonist of the story. Available for both body types.
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/3318c06131f4aa28775eda6eb7b8bc74025bb43e.png[/img]
[h3]2 new Faces[/h3]
Say hello to the old hag (or the friendly sage) with the new old face options for both male and female body types.
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/50314cba59c08decc071679600b4293fde4f00db.png[/img]

[h2]⚙️ Improvements and Fixes[/h2]
[list]

[b]New Features & Improvements[/b]
[*] Maps can now save and load the mood & lighting setting that was set while saving the map file.
[*] Death saves have been added to the character sheets. They can be used when the HP of a character goes down to 0 and will correctly react to critical fail or saves. (They can also be added/removed manually)
[*] The LFG Button on PC now opens a confirmation popup before opening Discord
[*] Improved the collider on the "Rock" asset to be more precise.

[b]Fixes[/b]
[*] Fixed a rare bug where the "Add to Combat" and "Remove from Combat" Button stopped working.
[*] Fixed the icons in the submenu tab for the Miniaturebrowser being offset in VR.
[*] Fixed a visual bug in the public game browser that would show 2 texts on top of each other for the first entry.
[*] Fixed a bug where miniatures could miss animations when possessed by a player that did not spawn them 
[*] Fixed potential map migration errors for map files that were created before the Chapter 3 release.
[*] Fixed a bug where objects could get stuck in other players' hands.
[/list]

[h2]🫵Your Review matters![/h2]
Again, thank you, everyone, so much for your feedback and your support over the last weeks, it truly means a lot to us! 
If you want to support the game, [b]please leave a review on our Steam Page[/b]. It helps us and the game [u]immensely[/u]!
 
Player Edition:
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2839600/Dungeon_Full_Dive_Player_Edition/]https://store.steampowered.com/app/2839600/Dungeon_Full_Dive_Player_Edition/[/url]
GM Edition:

notes.notes:

As our community continues to grow, we've been closely listening to your feedback and bug reports. We've been actively engaging with everyone on our [url=https://discord.gg/e8FznWcyxk]Discord[/url], answering questions & comments, and of course, exchanging with our [b]fantastic community members.[/b]

[h2]💰Player Questionnaire: Win 20$![/h2]
We love to hear all your thoughts & feedback and to give everyone the chance to participate we have just released a new Player Questionaire for DFD and its development roadmap. 
Participate now to [b] shape the future of DFD[/b] and to secure your chance to [b]win a 20 $ Steam Gift Card[/b]! (One random participant will be selected).

[url=https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=bljfwshOhE2ZPmn9l5HkH6VRkJPcaeVHkvEu-QrZQUFUQjhVREJaOU9GSEpYMkM2Q1BIQ1pBVEcwTy4u][b]<<Take the Survey>>[/b][/url]

At the same time, our dev team has been hard at work to resolve any potential issues and to improve your player experience. So, we're thrilled to unveil yet another update just in time for your upcoming weekend gaming sessions!

Here is what's in this week's update:

[h2]🗺️ A New Map: Breeze Islands[/h2]

[i]"Breeze Island" is a tiny Island notable for its many Windmills. A small market and mountainous terrain offer a good starting point for some adventuring.[/i]

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44910592/5477230c8b255a6a19dae688d3e29439302531d1.png[/img]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44910592/c6968b4e7c0a61d8337d091b2579f10ccd0144c2.gif[/img]

[h2]⚙️ Improvements and Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[b]UI / UX[/b]
[*] Improved sorting logic for entries of the Map Browser.
   My Maps Tab: Entries are now sorted by last changed ascending.
   Official Map Tab: Entries are now sorted by name ascending.
   Public Map Tab: Entries are now sorted by likes descending.

[*] Improved sorting logic for entries of the Character Browser
   My Characters Tab: Entries are now sorted by last changed ascending.
   Official Characters Tab: Entries are now sorted by name ascending.

[*] Added a new Info Popup when attempting to access character sheets of miniatures, that are owned by other players.
[*] Improved the "unavailable" message inside the context menu "Full Dive" option, when attempting to Full Dive into a miniature that is not available for Full Dive,

[b]Charactersheet[/b]
[*] Corrected the AC Calculation for heavy armor
[*] Corrected the AC calculation for unequipping armor

[b]Gameplay[/b]
[*] Fixed a bug where the context menu could become non-responsive (for example after deleting a map asset)
[*] Fixed some floating assets on the "Elder Dragon Lair" Map.
[*] Fixed some floating assets on the "Winter Festival" Map.
[*] Fixed a Bug where the hover outline of a miniature could get stuck (after Full Dive).
[*] Fixed a Bug where players were able to Full Dive into miniatures using the context menu even if they were missing rights.


[b]Miscellaneous[/b]
[*] Updated the in-game newsboard with the new player survey.

[/list]

As always thank you for playing, we hope you enjoy your time in DFD and we look forward to hearing your feedback, thoughts, and ideas!

[b]See you inside Dungeon Full Dive![/b]

[h1]Greetings Adventurer! [/h1]

This is our first larger patch after the first week of the launch of the Player Edition!

First and foremost we want to say "Hello" to all the new players: 
Thank you for playing DFD, for bringing in your new ideas, for your awesome interactions on our discord, and of course for all of your feedback!

[url=https://discord.gg/e8FznWcyxk][img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/d776b95ce3951c6b6035941e94c532768f156bd1.gif[/img][/url]

Having said that, let's get into this week's content:
[h1]🗺️New Assets![/h1]

[h2]1. New Map: Highland Ruins[/h2]
We have added a brand new map to the official map tab called "Highland Ruins".

[i]In the "Highland Ruins" a mountainous path leads to an ancient ruin that isn't as uninhabited as it initially seems.[/i]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44910592/73bd1c10b64a41659fd2ecc15c87b3b5d1c2936b.png[/img]

[list]
[*] If you want to see the creation process behind the map and also get some [b]neat map-building tricks [/b] from the devs, you can check out our art team's creation process behind the map over here:
[previewyoutube=p4DLbISjQII;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]
[/list]


[h2]2. New Map: Elder Dragons Lair[/h2]

[i]Expanding on the "Vulcano Map", the "Elder Dragons Lair" Map is the final confrontation with an ancient beast. Multiple paths lead through these dangerous crumbling ruins in the midst of a volcano. The ultimate test of bravery and perseverance![/i]

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44910592/053caf6edfa73e47345f893b2cf0ba4483d0e40e.png[/img]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44910592/ce78a828ae50e59f8f6e5179adfb924beda4f80d.gif[/img]

[h1] 🔧 Fixed Issues[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed a bug where players could get scorpion legs after map change if they were crawling during the map change
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44910592/ee76ff2dd838315844db25f1d1a4cdcbca8e9caf.gif[/img]
[*] Fixed dice, rolled by tabletop players still generating sound effects even when you're in Full Dive mode and unable to see them.
[*]Fixed a rare bug where the hover HP bar could be visible in the main menu
[/list]

Thank you so much for playing DFD. Without you, none of this would be possible and your support is what allows us to bring DFD to the next level! 

[b]See you inside DFD![/b]

[b]P.S. What maps do you want to see in the next update? Let us know down below in the comments![/b]

[h3]Our team is proud to announce that Dungeon Full Dive is coming to Steam in Early Access on the 23rd of October! [/h3]

Become a cunning Tiefling rogue sneaking your way through deadly goblin camps, a charismatic Halfling bard charming and performing your way through town, or a battle-hungry barbarian charging deep into enemy flanks on the open field of battle. 
From the 23rd of October, you can bring your adventures to life inside Dungeon Full Dive, check out how the game looks right now here:

[previewyoutube=wv3p06i4ea8;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Playtest Dungeon Full Dive with your Friends, 1 Week before Early Access!

notes.title: The Closed Alpha is coming! + Win some Alpha Keys! – Developer Update
notes.notes:
[h3][b]Greetings, Travelers! [/b][/h3]

The year is coming to an end, and the Christmas season is calling. An eventful year lies behind us and we would like to thank you once again for all the support you have shown us. 2023 will not only be a more than thrilling year full of adventures for us, but also for you: the players. In this regard, we would like to send you off into the new year with anticipation and excitement: 

 
[h3][b]The closed Alpha is coming![/b] [/h3]

We are delighted to tell you that we have scheduled our Alpha playtest: It will take place on the 26.-29. of January! The first playtest for Dungeon Full Dive will be playable via Steam and available for our Kickstarter Backers and late pledgers.

[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/039/519/745/60e51c00eb656191d1a387bffdca7eb4_original.png?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1671801999&gif-q=50&lossless=true&s=969342bafa54fe7c0165bd7f8ac88dfc[/img]
 
What kind of features can you expect in the Alpha? 
 
[list]
[*] [b]Play with your friends [/b]
Jump into the DFD multiplayer with your party, chat with your friends and roll the dice. 
[*] [b]Explore the World from the eyes of your miniature [/b]
Explore the world in VR (or with mouse and keyboard) from the tabletop perspective or jump into your character and interact with a variety of objects right inside your world. 
[*] [b]Edit your Hero [/b]
Try out an early version of the character creator and switch up your style with a first batch of character assets. 
[*] [b]Build your maps [/b]
Build your first maps with the first iteration of the map editor: Browse through assets and place them into your world to make it come alive. (Or scale up your Fighters Longsword to 5m, because everyone needs one of those).
Adjust the lighting and switch from day to night to set the mood.
[/list] 

With our first alpha playtest, we want to give you the chance to provide us with your valuable feedback regarding the mechanics of DFD, as you will be able to test some of the first versions of the core features. 

The alpha playtest is an exclusive early look at the game for our supporters and our first playtest at a large scale. Keep in mind, features are still missing while other might change (based on your feedback) and even though our QA is doing their best job to find every possible bug, there is only so much we can find on our own. So, expect there to be bugs and some rough edges here and there. 

But worry not, we have prepared different ways for you to provide us with your feedback and findings (more on this coming soon) during the alpha. 

However, for the reasons above this first playtest will be under an NDA. This means that you will not be able to show public footage of this early version of Dungeon Full Dive for now. 
[h3]
[b] Haven’t been able to get an alpha key yourself? This is your chance to claim some alpha keys![/b][/h3]

[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/039/519/751/bd0344b3144265548a2483f7af223b12_original.png?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1671802087&gif-q=50&lossless=true&s=3e82cefbaf67e054b1fbb1eeefb6585a[/img]

If you missed the chance to secure yourself an Alpha code (or you want to get additional codes for your party members) head over to our [url=https://twitter.com/DungeonFullDive/status/1606365123752341504]Twitter channel[/url]!  

While you are reading this, we have just started a giveaway where you can snag yourself a package of 5 codes for the Alpha! All you have to do is post the best (or worst?) rendition of your D&D character drawn in Paint (or any other digital drawing software) and you have a chance to win! 

And don’t worry: the winner will not be chosen based on artistic skill. One winner will be chosen at random, while the other will be the community favorite (measured by likes & retweets) - Have fun! 

You can also expect many more teasers of the alpha coming soon, so to never miss any of our updates  head over to our social media channels and sign up to our Newsletter. You can find all of our channels [url=https://linktr.ee/txk_gaming]here[/url].  

In addition, we are currently planning an open beta in 2023, so that even more people can take the opportunity to play the game and send us feedback. Stay tuned for more information on this! 


We also wanted to quickly recap 2022 in this last community update of the year.   


[h3]In 2022... [/h3]

 
... the TxK Gaming family has grown considerably. Our amazing team was able to level up by welcoming additional, talented industry veterans, who all work eagerly to make DFD an even greater experience for you.  

We also owe this to the additional funding for our project, which we received this year from the federal grant for video game developers ("Computerspielförderung"). And so, we are on our best way to provide you with the truly immersive tabletop experience we all are striving for. 

As many of you have probably already seen, Dungeon Full Dive can be found on Steam.  

If you missed this update and want to support us, wishlist DFD on Steam as our release window for mid of 2023 grows closer! (Every wishlist helps us out a ton!) 

 

This wraps up our community recap for the end of 2022. We can't wait to start this exciting new year with you! 

 

Until then, 

The whole TxK Gaming team wishes all of you a happy holiday season and a wonderful start 

into 2023! 🎅 🎆 

 

~Your TxK Gaming Team

notes.title: Our Character Editor! #2 - Developer Update
notes.notes:
[h2][b]Our Character Editor! #2 - Dressed for the occasion[/b][/h2]
[b]Greetings Travelers! [/b]

Welcome back to our latest developer update and the second part of the [b]character editor[/b] [b]insight series[/b], in which we are giving you a look behind the curtains of our character art pipeline as well as its main challenge: Creating a [b]gorgeous-looking[/b], visual art style for our characters, while at the same time meeting the[b] strict performance goals[/b] that we set ourselves (to ensure good performance for all of our players). 

While in the last part of the series ([url=https://txkgaming.com/uncategorized/our-character-editor-1-development-update/]#1 The visual art challenge: Bringing your heroes to life[/url]), we investigated the visuals of our characters, in this part we will focus on the [b]features of the character editor[/b] as well as the [b]technical details[/b] that come along with it. 

[b]So, let’s dive right into it! [/b]

[h2][b]The Technical Setup [/b][/h2]
To build the fundamentals of our character editor, we first had to determine the parts of the character that we wanted to be able to modify. So, we started by defining separate regions on the characters' face and their body, that should be [b]swappable[/b]. These regions include [b]body features like hair, eyes, and ears[/b], as well as[b] clothing[/b] such as [b]chest[/b] [b]pieces, gauntlets, or boots. [/b]
[img]https://txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-1.png[/img][i]Barbarian clothing zones[/i]

Another fundamental decision that we made for our character editor was that the [b]clothing pieces should fit all classes[/b]:

[u]If a wizard wants to wear heavy chainmail, why not let them?[/u] 

Now, with our zones identified, we were able to [b]swap out each of them individually[/b]. In theory, our characters can now mix and match their outfits with different hairstyles, chest pieces, boots, gauntlets, etc.

[b]Character editor completed & adventure finished? [/b]
Sadly, far from it! With this system in place there are two main issues that still exist and need solving:
[olist][*][b]Layered clothing [/b][/*][/olist][olist][*][b]Performance [/b][/*][/olist]
So, let’s take a deeper look into these two problems: [b]Why do they exist and how did we solve them?[/b] 

[h2][b]Layered clothing [/b][/h2]
When we compare our existing barbarian design with the design of this monk over here, we can already see one [b]fundamental difference:[/b] 

[img]https://txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/MonkZonesComparedColoredLines-1024x655.png[/img][i]Barbarian vs Monk > Clothing zones compared[/i]

The zones we have defined for the barbarian are [b]completely[/b] [b]different[/b] [b]in size [/b]compared to the monk. Not only are the monk’s sandals much shorter ([b]barely going above the ankle[/b]), than the barbarian’s boots (almost[b] reaching up to the knee[/b]), but the barbarian’s boots are also much thicker than the monk’s sandals! Now, what would happen if we simply swapped out the barbarian’s boots with the monk’s sandals? 

By default, if we would swap out the boots with the sandals, there would be [b]missing information[/b] for the shin region, leading to a rather disturbing result: 

[img]https://www.txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-5-1024x749.png[/img][i]The barbarian is wearing the monk's sandals... but wait: the barbarian's pants aren't made for this![/i]

 Of course, the [b]easiest solution[/b] here would be to simply[b] disallow shoes to come in different sizes[/b]! That would mean [b]creating a system where all clothing pieces are of the same size[/b].

While a system like this would fix the problem and is also [b]commonly used in other games,[/b] we wanted to push the amount of flexibility not only for our artists but also for the players, when designing their characters. So that [b]we can allow a wider variety of character designs[/b]: 

[img]https://txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/MonkZonesComparedwBoxes-1024x655.png[/img][i]Different Concepts > Different Zones[/i]

So, after investing some time into R&D we came up with a much more [b]flexible solution:[/b]

[b]Layered Clothing[/b] 

By creating a layered clothing system, we allowed our clothing assets to be created [b]independently[/b] of the region's sizes.

That means that our[b] artists can create overlapping clothing pieces[/b] (e.g., very high boots, very long pants) and [b]dynamically cut away the unwanted areas of each clothing piece depending on the other equipped clothes.[/b] 

Normally overlapping clothes create frequent clipping (see image below), but by tagging each component with identifiers as well as a thickness level, we can compare these thickness levels and [b]cut away the thinner component.[/b]

In the following example, the boots are thicker than the pants, so the pants should be tucked into the boots. Without a layered clothing system, the pants and boots would look like this: 

[img]https://txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image.png[/img]
[i]The pants and boots are “clipping” into each other[/i]

In our case, the layered clothing system that we have created [b]automatically hides[/b] the pants at the region, where they would intersect!

[img]https://www.txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-3-1024x831.png[/img][i]The pants are tucked inside the boots[/i]

While this looks quite simple, the system actually needs to do quite A LOT of [b]technical-art-magic<sup>tm</sup>[/b] to handle all the edge cases that come along with the layered clothing (What happens if you have skin showing through a clothing piece? What happens to assets that vary in thickness [b]within[/b] their own region: e.g., a knight’s gauntlet that has very thick hand elements but only thin cloth elements above the wrist?)

Nevertheless, our team was able to overcome all of those challenges and we are very happy with the current pipeline and its flexibility regarding layered clothing. [b]Awesome job everyone! [/b]

However, with this issue solved, there was yet another main problem to be tackled: 
[h2][b]Performance[/b][/h2]
“This all sounds very cool and customizable but will it run without burning through my graphics card?” you may ask. 

It is very true that [b]performance is critical[/b], especially for VR games. Thus, a lot of thought went into the process of optimizing our characters and their clothing. Given that optimization is a [b]completely[/b] different topic in itself, we want to focus on the main bottleneck with this system: [b]Draw calls.[/b] 

[b][u]“What are draw calls?” [/u]I hear you asking.[/b] 

A great indicator of the performance cost is how often the [b]CPU [/b](Processor) [b]has to tell the GPU [/b](Graphics Card) how and where to draw meshes on the screen, usually referred to as “draw calls”. Since those commands to the GPU are quite expensive, when it comes to performance, you try to [b]reduce[/b] them as much as possible. 

Now, that our characters are made up of almost dozens of individual meshes, stitched together, you can already see where the problem is: Our character who [b]was just 1 draw call [/b]before now needs over 10 draw calls for each of their regions! Additionally, each “material” (the textures that give colors and patterns to our character) requires 1 additional draw call, leading to [b]a sum of around 20 draw calls! [/b] 

This means with [b]10 characters[/b] on screen we would have [b]almost 200 draw calls instead of 20[/b] (including draw calls for the materials)! 

While the example above is quite simplified the main issue is clear: [b]we need to reduce the draw calls! [/b] 

[b]So, what did we do? [/b] 

We were able to lower the number of draw calls to a minimum by [b]combining the textures and meshes[/b] of our character. This means that instead of one or more draw calls for every region (which would be the case if every region had its very own texture or mesh), the CPU issues [b]just two draw call[/b] for the whole character!

This combining does come at a cost though! While the [b]runtime performance[/b] (when actively playing) [b]is much better now[/b], the actual combining and merging of the character are fairly resource intense, which means additional loading times. However, the process of combining meshes and textures happens within the CPU itself. We can actively optimize it and run those calculations in parallel for a [b]significantly better performance! [/b] 

The result is a much more efficient character editor that can craft performant characters with [b]little to no loading times. [/b]

We could continue for hours about various technical details and optimizations that we deployed (like our solution for optimizing textures), however, given the length of this post already (comment [u]“Rolling constitution saving throw!” [/u]if you are still reading!) we will end this community update on this note. 

Nevertheless, we hope that this insight wasn’t too technical for you and that you enjoyed reading about our character editor! Of course, [b]we will be[/b] [b]active on Discord for feedback, questions, and just, in general, hanging out with you guys! [/b]

And if you haven't already: Don't forget to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1710740/Dungeon_Full_Dive/]wishlist DfD on Steam[/url] to support the development team! 

Thank you very much for reading this community update, and as always:

We are truly looking forward to seeing you inside DFD!

[b]- Your TxK Gaming Team [/b]

notes.title: Our Character Editor! #1 - Developer Update
notes.notes:
Greetings Travelers!

Welcome back to our latest developer update, where we give you a peek behind the curtains of development! In the last months, we have been heavily focusing on the	[b]		 map builder	[/b]	 as well as the	[b]		 character editor[/b]. Both of these topics are incredibly exciting for us to work on, and they both deserve a spot on their own in our developer updates.

	For this update, however, we want to take a [b]deeper look at our character editor[/b]. The reason for this is, that the work on the map builder has been strongly centered around optimization and improving our existing map asset pipeline: Technical essentials — that will enable us to make the most out of the players' hardware — which are, however, too technical for the moment (we will go into detail there, once the user-facing features are ready to be shown off as well!).

	So, without further ado, thank you for your patience, and let's start with this developer update!


[h1]	[b]		 Whether it's crawling through a dungeon or dancing at the queen's ball...	[/b][/h1]
	[b]		 ...our adventurers want to be dressed for the occasion!	[/b]

	This was our highest priority when we set up our character art pipeline. We want to allow players to not only equip different prebuilt outfits but to actually	[b]		 mix and match different, individual clothing pieces[/b] !

	Having this goal in mind we had to solve quite a lot of challenges. One of the biggest was defining a	[b]		 gorgeous-looking, visual artstyle	[/b]	 for our characters, while at the same time meeting the	[b]		 strict performance goals	[/b]	 that we have set up, to ensure a good performance for all our players.

	So how did we do it? For the sake of readability, we broke down the results of our work into two main parts for you:

	·	[b]		 #1 The visual art challenge:	[/b]	 Bringing your heroes to life

	And

	·	[b]		 #2 The development & technical art challenge:	[/b]	 Our clothing system


[h1]	#1 Bringing your heroes to life	[b]		 - An insight into the artstyle of our characters	[/b][/h1]
	Initially, when we started on the concepts for our characters and their outfits, we spent a lot of time finding the right level of	[b]		 stylization	[/b]	 and	[b]		 detail[/b]. We wanted our heroes to be the	[b]		 highlights of our fantasy worlds	[/b]	 and yet perfectly fit into the style of the environments.

	During the course of our conception phase, a	[b]		 wide variety of explorations and concepts[/b]	 had to be created, in order to get many different variations for our internal testing. Through this testing, we succeeded in achieving a fantastic final art style that we are proud to show off to you.

	So, let's accompany	[b]		 Dungeon Full Dive's barbarian outfit	[/b]	 on its journey through our character pipeline	[b]		 from concept art to 3D[/b]!

[h1]	2D - Exploration & Concept[/h1]
	The exploration phase is the first stage of conception, in which we	[b]		 wildly explore what is possible	[/b]	 for the outfit. This is done before we actually decide on a certain design that we want to implement. The results here are far from the final detailed design, and more focused on the	[b]		 general elements	[/b]	 that we want to have as well as the	[b]		 overall design[/b]. Things like the	[b]		 characters' silhouettes	[/b]	 are also very important during this stage!

	[b]		 Exploration	[/b]

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/087/c47109f19a39b7ee6d525a56877a52a7_original.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660473092&gif-q=50&q=92&s=62302b165ef6e1e6383c84b967c31b07[/img]	[u]		 
The first explorations are focused on finding the right clothing pieces and the overall design that we want to have.	[/u]

	[b]		 Concept	[/b]

	After we decide on the final elements for the outfit, our concept artists proceed with creating a first rendered concept art:

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/027/6a308ef8994a22556bb1a32bdc939c4e_original.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660471887&gif-q=50&q=92&s=cf2acda17c4de7e8e9937bed6cfb0b80[/img]	[u]		 
A more youthful look and pants! You can also see some explorations and thoughts on clothes, materials, and different armor pieces.	[/u]

	The further we proceed with the pipeline and the more we transition from 2D concept art towards the 3D plane, the more we have to consider the details of the design. When making a 3D character something very crucial comes into play:	[b]		 technical limitations	[/b]	 as well as the	[b]		 readability of the design[/b].

	That is why we must have an eye on things like the level of detail:

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/109/75b26c5fefa0d9d3f72db15feeeae526_original.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660473500&gif-q=50&q=92&s=7b08c0f9b13eb7602369a9432d33f5a4[/img]	[u]		
 More is not always better!	[/u]
[h1]	[b]		 3D	[/b]	 - Sculpting, Modeling & Texturing[/h1]
	[b]		 Sculpting	[/b]

	Next, based on the 2D concept, our 3D artists are able to sculpt a first model:

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/137/e386cccd4cf010cafe65b85a7b7c0659_original.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660474212&gif-q=50&q=92&s=fdf80e89d6c80850354617b5b3bbd0e6[/img]	[u]		 
The first translation in 3D with simple colors, to help with the visualization.	[/u]

	[b]		 Texturing	[/b]

	With a 3D model in place, we are able to texture the character. That means giving him color and bringing the materials to life!

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/148/68b03f01a667bfacf995d996f95928e6_original.png?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660474393&gif-q=50&lossless=true&s=774dc50c5be68385084aa2923db4ef27[/img]	[u]		 
We finally got a model we like! Nice! Unfortunately, we are not done yet. Now that we have the first version, we start on the details with lots of feedback from the other artists and developers.	[/u]

	Of course, during all of these steps, we also go through a feedback & polishing loop. The feedback & polishing is crucial for our artists, to	[b]		 reach our targeted visual goals[/b]! This is one example of such a feedback loop for the barbarian outfit:

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/268/325/402840cef146706ac0b9bface6aaab6b_original.png?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660429416&gif-q=50&lossless=true&s=8e67c9a87b4cb1679925cee11878dde8[/img]	[u]		 
There is a lot of thought and work that has to go into the creation of our characters!	[/u]

	After we review and discuss the changes, we can work them in, and our barbarian looks like this:

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/268/328/4078f3faa697d7f6ff54c87ccc287761_original.png?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660429453&gif-q=50&lossless=true&s=d9bd21835562eb19cd7168e8c8fbcd4c[/img]	[u]		
 Even more handsome, don't you think?	[/u]

	Now we can finalize the textures ...and add the final details!

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/477/097d793b0e7c1f3bf84eee0618653014_original.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660479062&gif-q=50&q=92&s=489d77da0177fc1ed1cfc2c0f52eb6c9[/img]	[u]		 
And there you go: Our barbarian is ready for the character editor, awesome! ... But what happened to the boots? This is explained in our technical-art-insight-post regarding the clothing system!	[/u]

	In summary, our outfits have to go through	[b]		 a lot of different stages	[/b]	 before being ready for the game: from exploration to the	[b]		 concept[/b], to	[b]		 sculpting[/b],	[b]		 texturing[/b], the	[b]		 feedback loop[/b], and final	[b]		 polishing!	[/b]

	[img]https://www.txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/FinalResult-1024x325.jpg[/img]	[u]		[u]			 As you can see, the design of the barbarian can drastically improve from one step to the next! And there are even more steps that we have not shown here for the sake of simplicity (like retopologizing, UV-layout, etc.). Making video games can be a tough job!		[/u]	[/u]

	I hope we were able to give you an	[b]		 insight	[/b]	 and understanding	[b]		 into our work[/b]! Keeping the length of this post and your reading pleasure in mind, we will have to continue the second part of this post in a separate community update. But worry not! It's already prepared and will be posted	[b]		 in the next weeks	[/b]	 ;)

	So, stay tuned for	[b]		 part 2[/b]: "The development & tech-art challenge: Our clothing system"

	In the meantime, feel free to let us know in the comments:	[b]		 What do you think of the design? What is the next class that you want to see?	[/b]

	And as always: We are truly looking forward to seeing you inside DFD!

	- Your TxK Gaming Team
